newsitem.title: INDIA: India flash floods toll 110, likely to reach 150.
newsitem.headline: India flash floods toll 110, likely to reach 150.

text.p: At least 110 people have been killed in Tuesday's flash floods that hit a remote Himalayan region in northern India, and the toll could rise to as much as 150, a senior police official said.

"I have a list of 110 persons (dead victims) who have been identified so far," a senior police official of the state of Himachal Pradesh told Reuters by telephone on Wednesday. "I suspect the toll could be much higher. It could even be 150, when reports come from cut-off areas," he said.

Authorities had said on Tuesday that at least 135 people were missing and feared dead after monsoon rains triggered the flooding in the Chirgaon region, some 125 km (80 miles) east of the state capital of Shimla.
The police official said a five square km (two square mile) lake had formed due to the floods at Wangtu, some 200 km (125 miles) east of Shimla by the River Sutlej on the highway to Tibet.

The official, who did not want to be identified, said the state's administration had cautioned the authorities managing the Bhakra Nangal Dam, built on the Sutlej in the down-river state of Punjab, of possible flooding.
The official said 12 villages in the Shimla and Kinnaur districts of the state had been submerged.
